title: Parameters and Arguments
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of Parameters and Arguments and define its core vocabulary.
Apply parameters and arguments in a small PowerShell example and predict its result.
Identify one relevant edge case, version constraint, or troubleshooting step.

content.intro: This lesson covers Parameters and Arguments in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Reliable scripts use an explicit parameter contract, a predictable output contract, and dependencies relative to `$PSScriptRoot` rather than the caller’s current directory. Reusable functions validate input and make changes previewable with `SupportsShouldProcess`, `-WhatIf` and `-Confirm` when appropriate.

content_blocks.title: Build understanding step by step
content_blocks.text: Start with the syllabus concepts: Positional script arguments; The param() block; Mandatory versus optional parameters; Supplying parameters from command lines. Separate the input, the operation and the expected result. Use a disposable local workspace for file or system examples, and verify platform-specific behavior against the active runtime.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Review this snippet as a static teaching example. In a local PowerShell 7.6 session, save a copy under your course workspace, run it manually, and compare the result with the stated expectation. CodeLeaf’s current course preview does not execute PowerShell. Adjust environment-dependent output to your machine.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Check command availability with Get-Command, inspect values with Get-Member, consult Get-Help -Full, and verify PowerShell version/platform before assuming identical output. Do not run examples that change system state without adapting and reviewing them.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and use synthetic values. If you created test files, delete only those files within the dedicated practice folder after checking their paths.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.

content.task: Try it yourself: design a reusable interface with explicit inputs and outputs. Use synthetic data or a disposable practice folder, write down your predicted result, check it locally, and explain one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central idea in Parameters and Arguments in your own words.
Verify the expected result using a local session or a documented manual check.
Describe one relevant edge case, limitation or troubleshooting step.
hints: Predict the output before changing the example.
Change one input or condition at a time and compare the results.
Use Get-Help and official versioned documentation when behavior differs; do not treat a static preview as execution.
